note_sections.t: Persistent PSA elevation and confirmation of Gleason 4+3 carcinoma on prior biopsy bucket "Positive" warrant clinical reassessment.

A 61-year-old retired bank clerk entered the diagnostic pathway in late 2023 due to elevated PSA levels. He is a non-smoker with a background of hypertension treated by valsartan and lisinopril, plus osteoarthritis managed with paracetamol PRN. Divorced, he resides in an assisted-living facility and enjoys tennis twice weekly, averaging 22 units of alcohol each week. With his daughter handling correspondence under consent, he recently completed baseline memory screening and a sleep clinic assessment for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. A prior 12-core biopsy confirmed Gleason 4+3 disease. He experiences chronic lower urinary tract symptoms yielding an IPSS of 20/35, yet denies urinary retention, haematuria, unexplained weight loss, or bone pain. His overall condition remains stable.

DRE — texture: moderately enlarged gland with a firm, discrete nodule palpable in the left peripheral zone; remainder symmetrically smooth without induration. General examination shows stable vital signs, unremarkable systemic findings, and no palpable lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.
